documents.name: GitHub
documents.description: Integrate with GitHub and receive related events
documents.instructions:
### Connect

GitHub asks you to accept the Flow app's permissions and to choose the organisation or account to install it into. When the installation finishes, GitHub returns you here and the app is linked to this workspace.

The app needs Issues: write, Pull requests: write, Contents: read or write, Commit statuses: write and Actions: write. Each GitHub task names the permission it uses. When the app's permissions change, an organisation owner approves them again on GitHub.

### After connecting

The GitHub trigger appears in a workflow's Configure tab, and chosen repositories' events start workflows. Switch on "Share the installation token with tasks" to let the GitHub tasks act as the app.

### Disconnect

Disconnect removes the link from this workspace and any parameters it shares here. The installation stays on GitHub until you remove it there.

fields.name: github-token
fields.label: GitHub token
fields.description: GitHub App installation token, refreshed by Flow every 45 minutes

fields.name: github-url
fields.label: GitHub API URL
fields.description: The GitHub API the installation token is for

documents.name: Slack
documents.description: Run workflows from Slack, and let the Slack tasks post and manage channels as the Flow app
documents.instructions:
### Connect

Slack asks you to choose the Slack workspace to install the Flow app into and to allow its permissions. Slack then returns you here with that Slack workspace connected to this one. Several Flow workspaces can connect the same Slack workspace.

The app asks for these bot scopes:
- `chat:write`, `commands`, `users:read`, `users:read.email`: the slash command that runs a workflow, and the find member tasks
- `channels:read`, `groups:read`: the get channel tasks
- `channels:manage`, `groups:write`: the create, delete, invite and remove channel tasks
- `files:write`: the upload file task

### After connecting

The app's slash command runs workflows from Slack. Switch on "Share the installation token with tasks" to let the Slack tasks post and manage channels as the app.

### Disconnect

Disconnect removes the link from this workspace only. Removing the Flow app inside Slack disconnects every Flow workspace that uses it.

fields.name: slack-token
fields.label: Slack token
fields.description: The Flow app's bot token for the connected Slack workspace

documents.name: Google
documents.description: Let the Google Sheets and Drive tasks act as a Google Cloud service account
documents.instructions:
### Connect

Have a Google Cloud service account ready:
- Create it in a project with the Google Sheets and Google Drive APIs turned on.
- Create a JSON key for it and paste the whole key file below.
- Share each spreadsheet or Drive folder the tasks use with the service account's email address.

Some organisations block service account key creation until an administrator lifts the policy.

### Disconnect

Disconnect removes the key from this workspace. Delete the key in the Google Cloud console as well if nothing else uses it.

fields.name: google-service-account-key
fields.label: Service account key (JSON)
fields.description: The whole JSON key file of the Google Cloud service account the tasks act as

documents.name: Microsoft
documents.description: Let the Teams and SharePoint tasks call Microsoft Graph as a Microsoft Entra app
documents.instructions:
### Connect

Have a Microsoft Entra app registration ready:
- Register an app in Microsoft Entra ID.
- Grant it the Microsoft Graph application permissions the Teams and SharePoint tasks need, and have an administrator grant consent.
- Create a client secret for it.
- Enter the directory (tenant) ID, the application (client) ID and the client secret below.

The tasks request their own Microsoft Graph tokens with these credentials.

### Disconnect

Disconnect removes the credentials from this workspace. Delete the client secret in Microsoft Entra ID as well if nothing else uses it.

fields.name: microsoft-tenant-id
fields.label: Directory (tenant) ID
fields.description: The Microsoft Entra directory the app is registered in

fields.name: microsoft-client-secret
fields.label: Client secret
fields.description: A client secret of the app registration
